findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` is true only for users who are both, so a plain admin, or an owner whose membership is not also flagged as admin, is denied. Separately, `teamId ?? 0` is queried for non-team events. The intent is clearly admin OR owner. This is a permissions bug.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to the booking
findings.body: Authorization passes if the caller's email matches any attendee, including a guest who was added earlier. Guests can then invite further people, and the organizer's calendar event and emails are triggered. The email comparison is also case-sensitive, and the handler does not check that the user's email is verified.

findings.title: Guest dedup and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive; no limit on guests
findings.body: Blacklisted emails are lowercased, but the guest value is compared as-is, so `Foo@x.com` bypasses the blacklist. The comparison against existing attendees is also case-sensitive. The duplicates inside the `guests` input are not removed server-side, and the array has no max length, so a single call can create an unbounded number of attendees and emails.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the raw `guests` input rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered list. Existing attendees or blacklisted addresses in the input are treated as new guests and receive the scheduled email again. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Calendar update is unguarded and runs after the DB write
findings.body: The DB update has already committed when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and the call is not in a try/catch. A calendar failure makes the mutation error out even though the guests were saved, and the emails are never sent. The EventManager is also built from `ctx.user` credentials, not the organizer's, which is wrong when the caller is an attendee or admin.

findings.title: New guests get the standard scheduled email, ignoring the event type's disabled-email settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` neither checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` nor accepts event type metadata, unlike the other senders. Emails are sent even when the event type disables them.

findings.title: Error toast message is built incorrectly
findings.body: The message is always a non-empty template string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never applies. The raw `err.data?.code` is also shown to the user, and `t(err.message)` is applied to arbitrary server messages. Also, `isInvalidEmail` is never reset after a successful retry.

findings.title: Add guests action is offered on all bookings, including past ones
findings.body: The item is placed in the shared `editBookingActions`, so it appears for past bookings, and for seated and recurring events, where adding attendees may be inappropriate. The label also reuses `additional_guests`, and the action id is named `add_members`.
